name: logo-tall-crest
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Presentation Attributes, Images: Embed
story: A designer drew a scorebug down the left edge with a tall club crest, a translucent dark backplate, and text layers for club and score, exported from Illustrator with presentation attributes and embedded images.
idioms: the placed tall crest is a POSITIONED <image> with x="170" y="150" width="140" height="220" and inline xlink:href data: URI
overflow="visible" on the <image>, which Illustrator writes on placed raster artwork
xlink:href rather than href, with xmlns:xlink declared on the root
Styling: Presentation Attributes - direct fill, fill-opacity, font-family, font-size and font-weight attributes instead of a <style> block with .stN classes
Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build, <?xml?> prolog, root attrs with x="0px" y="0px", fill="none", and style="enable-background:new 0 0 1920 1080;"
one nested <tspan x="340" y="..."> per text element
tab indentation matching Illustrator export formatting
a space in a layer name written as Illustrator's _x20_ escape (id="Bug_x20_backplate"), which is how every other Illustrator file in this corpus spells one
PostScript font names in quotes (font-family="'Archivo-Bold'") rather than the family name Figma writes
whyThisMatters: A tall club crest is a strongly vertical picture slot (140x220) embedded directly as a positioned image, and this file checks that Illustrator's presentation-attributes export exposes that raster as a swappable picture field beside the club and score text. It also pins the growth answer against the other scorebugs in the corpus, which state shrink: those are drawn as several overlapping plates with no single panel behind the words, while this one has one 420x260 backplate carrying the club name, so the whole ladder is what the designer should be offered. A scorebug is not automatically a fixed layout - what decides it is whether a rectangle behind the text can widen.
